summary: A grid of pieces of a few colours. Each move swaps two neighbouring pieces (side by side or one above the other) so that three or more pieces of one colour stand in a line. Those pieces are removed, the pieces above fall into their places and new pieces come in at the top; lines that form as they fall are removed too. A swap that lines nothing up is undone by the game.

cells.looks: one piece; its colour is what it is, whatever its shape or face
a place in the grid's outline that never holds a piece (a gap, a wall)
a cell hidden by an animation, a dialog or a piece in mid-fall

state_fields.grid: the grid's rows from the top, each a list of cells from the left: a piece is the number of its colour (1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue, 6 purple, 7 pink, 8 white, 9 cyan, 10 brown; the nearest of these, and always the same number for the same kind of piece), 0 a place that holds no piece, null a cell nobody read
state_fields.score: the game's score as read, or null
state_fields.scene: the id of the scene the screen shows

actions.description: drag the piece at `cell` onto its neighbour at `to` ([row, column] each)

scenes.looks: the grid at rest, waiting for a swap
the game's own message that the level or game is won
the game's own message that it is over (no moves or time left)

meta_actions.description: start another game or level after the end

colours.description: how many colours the game's own pieces come in (only the simulated game draws by it)
